title: Modified QuEChERS Method for PFAS in Environmental Biological Matrices
author: Yun, Kurz, et al.
materials: extraction from the matrix was incomplete,

Due to the complexity of the biological samples, some targeted compounds can be affected by the specific matrix. Based on our observations and comparisons, extraction of freeze-dried samples reduces matric effect (based on extraction standard recovery values) compared to extraction of wet samples. The improved extraction performance is more notable for some long chain length PFAS. In addition, inclusion of matrix spike samples is useful to evaluate the matrix effects as this provides information on mass-labeled and native analytes; if mass-labeled and native analytes are similarly affected (e.g., FTSs in goldfish), the isotope dilution can provide a reliable estimate. Furthermore, matrix effects can be reduced by increasing the extraction standard concentrations and decreasing injection volume, though this can create sensitivity issues (i.e., < LOQ) for compounds that are present in lower concentrations and /or for which the sensitivity is analytically lower (i.e., ionization and fragmentation).2)Method application

steps.title: Weigh and spike sample
steps.instruction: Place each biological sample (0.2–0.3 g dry weight (freeze‑dried) or 2 g wet weight (frozen)) into a 50 mL polypropylene centrifuge tube and add 100 µL of the mass‑labeled extraction standard mix MPFAC‑24 ES (stock 25 µg L⁻¹), delivering 2.5 ng of each extraction‑standard compound per sample.

steps.title: Add water and acetonitrile
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL LC/MS‑grade water, vortex for 10 s; then add 12 mL LC/MS‑grade acetonitrile and vortex for 30 s to obtain a homogeneous slurry.

steps.title: Add extraction salts and shake
steps.instruction: Add 1 g sodium chloride and 4 g magnesium sulfate to the tube and immediately shake vigorously by hand to prevent magnesium coagulation.

steps.title: Sonicate and centrifuge extraction
steps.instruction: Place up to 24 tubes in a bath sonicator set to 30 °C and sonicate for 1 h. Then centrifuge at 4000 rpm (maximum 3739 × g) for 30 min to separate layers (top acetonitrile, sample matrix, water, salts).

steps.title: Prepare cleanup sorbent mixture
steps.instruction: In a clean 15 mL polypropylene centrifuge tube add 200 mg end‑capped C18, 100 mg ENVI‑Carb, 50 mg primary‑secondary amine (PSA) and 1800 mg magnesium sulfate; mix gently.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant to cleanup tube
steps.instruction: Using a pipette, carefully transfer 10 mL of the top acetonitrile layer (supernatant) from the 50 mL extraction tube to the 15 mL tube containing the sorbents.

steps.title: Mix and centrifuge cleanup
steps.instruction: Manually shake the tube for 30 s, vortex for an additional 30 s, then centrifuge at 4200 rpm (maximum 4122 × g) for 30 min to separate the cleaned extract from the sorbent.

steps.title: Collect cleaned extract and evaporate
steps.instruction: Transfer 6 mL of the clear supernatant to a new 15 mL polypropylene tube and evaporate the solvent to dryness under a gentle stream of nitrogen.

steps.title: Reconstitute dried extract
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 mL of 0.1 % (v/v) acetic acid in methanol to the dried residue, sonicate for 10 min, then add 0.5 mL of 0.1 % acetic acid in LC/MS‑grade water and vortex for 10 s.

steps.title: Add injection standards and final spin
steps.instruction: Pipette 0.8 mL of the reconstituted solution into a new 2 mL microcentrifuge tube, add 0.2 mL of the mass‑labeled injection‑standard mix MPFAC‑C‑IS (5 µg L⁻¹, delivering 1 ng of each IS), vortex, and centrifuge at 13000 rpm (maximum 16200 × g) for 30 min.

steps.title: Transfer aliquot to LC vial
steps.instruction: Transfer 100 µL of the final supernatant to a polypropylene LC vial for analysis; store the remainder in a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube for archiving. The final sample pH is approximately 4.5.

steps.title: Prepare quality‑control samples
steps.instruction: For each batch of 24 samples include: 2 method blanks (empty vials), 2 laboratory control samples (empty vials spiked with the 24 target PFAS), 2 matrix‑spike samples (matrix spiked with the 24 PFAS at a mid‑level), and 1 SRM. Process all QC samples exactly as described for unknowns.

steps.title: Store samples and extracts
steps.instruction: Store biological samples at –20 °C, store extracts at 4 °C in 2 mL microcentrifuge tubes, and transfer to LC vials only immediately before analysis.

steps.title: LC‑QTOF analysis
steps.instruction: Inject 10 µL of each sample onto a Gemini C‑18 column (50 mm × 3 mm, 3 µm) with a Luna C18(2) delay column (30 mm × 3 mm, 5 µm) and a Gemini C18 guard column (4 mm × 2 mm). Operate the SCIEX ExionLC coupled to an X500R QTOF in negative ESI mode using scheduled high‑resolution MRMHR. Quantify PFAS by isotope dilution using the extraction standards. Run a solvent blank (0.1 % acetic acid in 50 % methanol:water v/v) every six samples, a calibration curve of ≥5 standards spanning at least a 20‑fold concentration range (R² ≥ 0.98), and initial/continuing calibration verifications (ICV/CCV) as described, ensuring extraction‑standard and injection‑standard recoveries are within 50‑150 % (QC acceptance criteria).
